Callie, an exceptional Sprocker Spaniel trained by Medical Detection Dogs, can detect stage 1 bowel cancer by sniffing human urine samples.

Working alongside researchers, she’s helping advance a non-invasive approach to finding colorectal cancer at its earliest and most treatable stage.

In trials, Callie identified the disease from samples as small as two milliliters. She can also distinguish the cancer’s unique scent from other bowel conditions, including Crohn’s disease, irritable bowel disease, and diverticulitis.

The research team hopes to use what they learn from Callie’s remarkable sense of smell to develop electronic “e-nose” diagnostic tools that could complement screening methods such as colonoscopies.

🌐 CoinDCX has confirmed losing 15.99 million USDT through compromised wallet infrastructure after initially rejecting claims that nearly $16 million had been stolen from the Indian cryptocurrency exchange. The exchange said a failure in its automated deposit-sweeping service allowed cryptocurrency to accumulate at an address that customers continued using despite instructions to switch to newer wallets. CoinDCX absorbed the resulting loss and maintained that customer balances and active trading systems were not affected.

⚠️ The admission follows several days of disagreement between CoinDCX executives and blockchain investigators over suspicious transactions involving wallets linked to the exchange. On October 22, CoinDCX CEO Sumit Gupta rejected suggestions of another security breach, saying the flagged addresses belonged to infrastructure compromised in July 2025. He maintained that no funds had moved from current operational wallets into the addresses under scrutiny.

📊 However, the company’s latest statement confirms that deposits continued arriving at those addresses and that its own systems were responsible for transferring them to secure wallets when the automated service functioned correctly. CoinDCX said it noticed unusual activity on October 21 but discovered irregular fund movements the following day through blockchain records and community reports.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

Lately, I've been interviewing AI Engineer candidates with 1–2 years of experience.

One thing surprised me.
Almost everyone can talk about RAG.
Almost everyone has built AI agents.

Most have used LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini.
But when the conversation moves beyond frameworks...
...that's where many interviews start to slow down.

I ask simple questions like:
"Why do embeddings work?"
"Why does chunk size affect retrieval?"
"Why does an attention mechanism matter?"
"What actually happens before an LLM generates the first token?"

The room usually goes quiet.
It made me realize something.
We're getting really good at building AI applications.

But we're slowly skipping the fundamentals that make those applications reliable.
AI tools can write code.
They can generate APIs.
They can even scaffold an entire project.

But they can't replace your understanding.
If retrieval quality drops...
If latency suddenly doubles...
If hallucinations increase...
If your AI agent gets stuck in a loop...

The solution isn't another framework.
It's understanding what's happening underneath.
Frameworks will change.
Models will change.
The fundamentals won't.

That's why, before every interview, I'd rather revise concepts like:
→ Transformers
→ Attention Mechanism
→ Embeddings
→ Tokenization
→ Vector Search
→ HTTP & APIs
→ System Design
→ Memory
→ Databases
→ Evaluation
→ Python fundamentals
These are the concepts that help you explain why something works, not just how to build it.

If you're preparing for AI Engineer interviews, don't spend all your time learning the next framework.
Spend some time strengthening the foundation that every framework is built on.

💬 First VP hails Iran’s growing role in regional blocs ahead of ECO summit

📌 Tehran, IRNA – First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref, referring to the country’s presence in regional blocs and unions, says Iran has been maintaining serious and effective participation in bodies such as the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).

Aref made the remarks on Saturday at a planning meeting for the upcoming summit of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), a Eurasian political and economic intergovernmental organization, which will be held in Tehran.
​
Stating that fostering engagement and expanding relations with regional nations is a key strategy of the current administration and, in particular, a priority for President Masoud Pezeshkian, he noted that Iran’s standing within regional groupings has improved significantly compared to the past.
​
He attributed the increased interactions and cooperation to Pezeshkian’s personal approach and style, as well as the performance of executive bodies and reciprocal positive moves by the regional countries.
​
Referring to the ECO meeting in Iran, he said experience has shown that the country achieves greater success in summits as a host, adding that officials from participating nations have consistently left Iran with a positive impression.
​
On the ECO itself, Aref expressed disappointment that the 10-nation organization — initially founded by Iran, Pakistan, and Turkey — has unfortunately not been able to perform as effectively as it should have since its inception in 1985.
​
He said the leaders of the member states need to expand their activities to enhance their collaboration within the ECO framework, enabling the organization to reclaim its proper regional standing.
​
Aref continued by noting that ECO members share deep historical and civilizational ties with Iran, providing a solid foundation for expanding regional cooperation, especially among nations across Central Asia, the Caucasus, and the region east of Iran.
​
ECO promotes economic, trade and transport cooperation among its 10 members, namely Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

Gold is widely considered the ultimate safe-haven asset. But something interesting is happening right now. Despite high oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and a falling stock market, gold itself has dropped to a three-month low, losing around 4% in a single week.

The reason is pretty simple. High oil prices are fueling inflation again. The higher inflation goes, the more likely the Fed is to keep interest rates elevated or raise them further. And gold doesn't generate any interest income on its own. When bonds and the dollar start offering more attractive returns, some money flows in that direction instead.

There's a second factor, too. When markets sell off sharply, investors sometimes have to sell just about everything to cover losses and meet margin calls. That's why even gold can temporarily fall alongside stocks during periods of severe market stress. And that's exactly the kind of price action we're seeing right now.

And here's the key takeaway. A safe-haven asset isn't necessarily an asset that rises during every crisis. Gold performs well against some risks and less well against others. It can provide protection against currency problems, debt crises, and financial instability, while simultaneously coming under pressure from high interest rates and a strong dollar.

That's why it's worth rethinking gold as an all-purpose hedge. Before buying any safe-haven asset, it is important to first understand exactly which risk needs to be hedged. Because the very same crisis can make gold either the best-performing asset in portfolio or, at least temporarily, one of the worst.
